lots.dropped_entries: Down East magazine 'appraisal USD 200-300': page returns HTTP 403, snippet only, unclear which instrument, and an appraisal is not a sale; dropped. lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: gilt fallboard 'Mason & Hamlin BOSTON U.S.A.' clearly read. Photo 4: retailer stencil '...INDLAY & CO...' over 'LAUNCESTON HOBART', partly cropped and worn, a nice Tasmanian provenance point. About 4 octaves, ivory or bone naturals with some chips and dirt, ebony sharps, red-stained key fascia. Line-strung walnut case, carrying handle on the end, two felt-covered pedals on cords to the bellows. Dusty, finish wear on the top rail, scuffs on the stand.
lots.condition: Dusty and worn finish, keys dirty with minor chipping, pedal covers worn; reeds and bellows untested. Looks complete.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does it play: do both pedals raise wind and do all keys sound (any dead notes or leaking bellows)? Is anything missing, such as a lid or music rest?

lots.question_for_armitage: Is the framed Broadwood price list (sticker '5050/5 + Piano') included with this lot? Does the piano play and hold any tuning, and is there a serial number on the frame or wrest plank? Are the keys ivory (this affects resale and export)?
